Use "I" statements—e.g., "I’ve been having trouble sleeping and concentrating after late-night gatherings"—then propose concrete rules like no guests after 10pm on weeknights or limiting late-night visitors to one night a week with advance notice.

Example script: "Can we talk? I want to avoid conflict, but if we can’t reach a compromise I’ll need to involve the landlord or consider other housing options."

If they get defensive or minimize, stay calm, acknowledge their perspective briefly (“I get you like having people over”), then firmly restate the impact with an “I” statement and the specific ask (“I need guests gone by 10pm on weekdays”) and request a yes/no or a time to decide.  
If you feel yourself freezing, keep a short script on your phone to read or say, “I’m overwhelmed right now—can we pause and talk in 30 minutes?” so you can regroup.  
If they agree but later slip up, document dates/times, send a calm message referencing the agreement and the specific infractions, and ask for a corrective plan plus a follow-up check-in.  
If the behavior continues, put the rules in a written roommate agreement or request mediation/landlord involvement, and start exploring other housing options while framing any move as a personal need for quiet rather than a threat.  
Decide ahead of time what consequence you’ll follow through on and actually follow it—consistency makes your boundary effective.

2) During: open with an “I” statement, acknowledge their perspective, state the boundary and ask for a yes/no or a time to decide, and propose a check-in in two weeks.

4) After: document any breaches (dates/times/messages) and if they slip, send a calm written reminder referencing your agreement and request a corrective plan before the check-in.
